segments.title: Mikasa as a living museum ship
segments.summary: Two busy days aboard Mikasa show how visitors and welcoming staff keep a preserved warship socially active, including Japanese guests and U.S. Seventh Fleet personnel who came to meet the ShipShape team.
segments.body: Mikasa was busy with visitors of different ages on both days of the visit. The staff made the experience welcoming, while Japanese visitors and personnel from the U.S. Seventh Fleet came to meet the ShipShape team. Their presence gives the preserved warship the atmosphere of an active public meeting place rather than a static exhibit. This moment captures the social life around a museum ship and the international audience that Mikasa draws.

evidence.note: Clarke describes the visitors, staff, and reception aboard Mikasa.
